chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Double-time saxophone from Bechet and Barney Bigard
summary: Smith says his double-time playing came from Sidney Bechet and clarinetist Barney Bigard.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Now, one of the things that you're famous for as a player was this business of introducing the double-time into saxophone solo work. You were one of the people who was ahead in that. Would it be right to suggest that you started to get hold of this idea from listening to Sidney Bechet? Because he used to do that.
Yeah, that's right. Mmm-hmm. Sidney Bechet. For a saxophone, first the soprano sax, then I picked up... I loved that clarinet playing by Barney Bigard. Those were my two men.
Oh yes. Yeah, Barney Bigard was more modern.
